title.narrative: Transforming Seaweed Farming for Enhanced Food Systems in Zanzibar

description.narrative: By 2028, an estimated 15,000 seaweed-farming households in Kaskazini Unguja and Kaskazini Pemba, Zanzibar, are expected to achieve a 40 per cent increase in income through the transformation of seaweed farming from a subsistence activity into a dynamic and sustainable economic sector. This transformation will be enabled by integrated and closely coordinated United Nations support and driven by integrated financial solutions, value addition strategies, cooperative development and improved access to structured markets. The initiative will primarily benefit women and young people, who form the majority of seaweed farmers, enabling them to achieve sustainable livelihoods and actively participate across the entire value chain. It will thus advance gender equality and promote the inclusion of youth in the blue economy. By fostering economic resilience and reducing poverty among coastal populations, the programme will contribute to economic diversification, climate resilience and food systems transformation in line with Zanzibar Vision 2050 and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development—particularly Sustainable Development Goals 1, 2, 5, 8, 13, 14 and 17. Opportunities for scaling up local solutions are anticipated in similar coastal areas, including Mafia Island, Lindi, Tanga and the Coastal Region of the mainland Tanzania.
